description: The NOAA Continuously Operating Reference Stations Network (NCN), managed by NOAA's National Geodetic Survey, provides GNSS carrier phase and code range data from fiducial geodetic stations across the United States and its territories for three-dimensional positioning, meteorology, space weather and geophysics. The stations are independently owned and operated by hundreds of government, academic and private organisations, which share their data and station metadata with NGS; NGS analyses and distributes them free of charge. Data are available since 9 February 1994 in RINEX format, most within an hour of recording, with station coordinates, logs, time series plots and a custom request service (UFCORS). The archive is mirrored on the Registry of Open Data on AWS (bucket noaa-cors-pds, with RINEX from 1994 to 2026, raw data, coordinates and station logs). Coverage: the United States and territories, plus some partner sites abroad. Format and access: RINEX files by day and station through the NGS server, UFCORS and Amazon S3, free of charge and without restrictions as NOAA data. Caveats: stations change over time; users need GNSS processing software; hardware and operators differ. Simulation uses: reference positioning and timing infrastructure whose availability underpins surveying, precision agriculture, transport and timing; signals for ionospheric and space weather effects; and monitoring of ground motion at infrastructure. Related records: IGS products give the global network; the University of Bergen and Indonesian ROTI datasets derive ionospheric indices from similar receivers.
